Foreign-SAP 64-bit atomics for the SHMEM ring (WP-SHMEM A3/A4). SBCL: cas-sap-u64 (sb-ext:cas over sb-sys:sap-ref-64; returns PREVIOUS value), atomic-incf-sap-u64 (CAS-retry fetch-add; returns NEW value, wraps 2^64), load-sap-u64/store-sap-u64 (sb-sys:sap-ref-64) — test pal-sap-atomics 5/5 PASS. CLASP: documented NFR-PORT gap — Clasp has NO usable hardware atomic over a raw foreign cell. Probed (A4): mp:cas / mp:atomic-incf REJECT a cffi:mem-ref place at compile time (NOT-ATOMIC: 'Don't know how to atomically access the place (MEM-REF ...)'); the only foreign-backed primitive, core:acas on a (unsigned-byte 64) static-vector, SILENTLY DROPS THE STORE when the compare operand exceeds most-positive-fixnum (CAS 2^64-1 -> 5 returns the right prev but leaves memory unchanged) — disqualifying for ring tokens/sequence numbers that cross 2^62. So on Clasp cas-sap-u64 / atomic-incf-sap-u64 signal PAL-UNIMPLEMENTED and the SHMEM lock-free ring stays SBCL-only; Clasp cleanly falls back to UDP (a later *shmem-enabled* guard wires the transport selection). load-sap-u64 / store-sap-u64 ARE implemented on Clasp (cffi:mem-ref :uint64; load masked to unsigned because Clasp's :uint64 mem-ref sign-extends a high-bit-set word). Test pal-sap-atomics skips on Clasp (impl-name guard) -> clean T. SBCL green, Clasp green; ADR 0013 Clasp-status note records the gap. SHMEM transport roundtrip (Phase B) is DONE — see the FR-XPORT-2 transport row below; the v1 ring uses a mutex-guarded lane claim so it needs NO foreign-SAP CAS (these A3 SAP atomics stay valid PAL primitives kept for a future lock-free-MPSC ring, unused by the v1 ring; the real fence IS used). SHM-CREATE NFR-PORT GAP (Clasp/macOS-arm64, 2026-06-14): shm_open's variadic mode_t cannot be reliably passed by Clasp's CFFI on macOS arm64 — VERIFIED flaky (~40% failure across :uint/:int/:u32/:long); the created object is then unre-openable. A load-time C shim was tried (cc -shared at load) and REJECTED by the owner (build-time cc dependency). DECISION: take the gap — %shm-open-create is per-impl in pal-net.lisp (SBCL: foreign-funcall-varargs, verified correct every platform; Clasp: plain foreign-funcall, correct on Linux's register varargs ABI, UNRELIABLE on macOS arm64). So Clasp/macOS uses UDP; SBCL has full SHMEM everywhere; Clasp/Linux SHMEM is EXPECTED to work via plain foreign-funcall, PENDING verification on a Linux host. run-pal-shm-test tolerates the by-name attach failure ONLY on (and (eq pal-impl-name :clasp) (uiop:os-macosx-p)) (runtime check, not a reader conditional) and still creates+maps+detaches cleanly -> T; the MAP_SHARED second-mapping assertion stays unconditional. Mirrors [[clasp-threading-gap]]/[[clasp-sap-atomics]].

Method: SHMEM intra-host transport (WP-SHMEM, same-host auto-select + UDP fallback)
Artifact: src/dds-xport/shmem.lisp; src/dds-disc/{dataplane,disc}.lisp; src/dds-rtps/discovery.lisp; dds-tests shmem-{ring-init,lane-claim,enqueue,drain,drain-resource-guard,locator-wire,transport,receiver-thread,stress,end-to-end}; scripts/shmem-roundtrip.sh (make shmem-xproc); src/dds-bench/ (make bench-shmem)
Notes: WP-SHMEM Task F-series DONE 2026-06-14 (ADR 0013). Same-host intra-host transport delivering the IDENTICAL serialized RTPS datagrams through a POSIX mmap ring instead of UDP; engine UNTOUCHED (constructs the frozen dds.xport:transport record; feeds the same %handle-datagram). Segment per receiver = [header | pthread PROCESS_SHARED mutex+cond+stop+parked notify block | K per-sender SPSC lanes]; lane claim is MUTEX-GUARDED (no foreign-SAP CAS -> SBCL+Clasp full parity at that layer); steady-state enqueue/drain are lock-free aligned-u64 store/load + a REAL release/acquire fence; CONDITIONAL (parked-flag, Dekker StoreLoad) wakeup so a busy receiver is not futex-signalled per message; pshared mutex/cond NOT named semaphores (sem_open undrivable from the Lisp runtime on macOS arm64). Selection (dds.disc): auto-routes same-host USER DATA over SHMEM iff the remote shares this node's host-uuid (MD5 of hostname, SPDP-advertised) AND advertised a SHMEM Locator_t (vendor kind 0x47420001) + PID_SHMEM_HOST_UUID (vendor 0x8040); the resolved dest is CACHED per remote (0 per-datagram alloc) and invalidated on re-discovery/lease-out. UDP IS THE FALLBACK and carries ALL discovery/metatraffic/HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK + every non-SHMEM case; a peer that does not understand the SHMEM kind ignores it (fail-open) and matches over UDP; cross-vendor SHMEM out of scope (no standard RTPS SHMEM wire format). Ring is an UNTRUSTED parser surface — every len/offset bounds-checked vs lane extents even at (safety 0) (NFR-SEC-POSTURE); lane/ring-full -> reject -> UDP fallback for that datagram, NEVER a GC-heap fallback (reliable sample repairs via HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK). Hot-path: send stays slot-read + funcall (FR-XPORT-5), enqueue is raw SAP writes, 0 bytes/sample steady-state on the SHMEM send path (gate-hotpath + make mem cover it; the gated XCDR codec is already 0-alloc). TESTS (all green SBCL): shmem-ring-init/lane-claim/enqueue/drain/drain-resource-guard (ring unit), shmem-locator-wire (locator codec), shmem-transport/receiver-thread (transport + threaded receiver loopback), shmem-end-to-end (in-process disc-layer integration over SHMEM), shmem-stress (4 senders x 5000 distinct -> exactly 20000 delivered, no loss/corruption/deadlock), the ring-record-parser fuzz (make fuzz: malformed len, wrap-sentinel edge, oversized record), make shmem-xproc (REAL 2-process cross-image round-trip — the proof loopback within one image cannot give), run-bench-shmem (make bench-shmem). BENCH (bench/report/2026-06-14-wp-shmem.md, SBCL/macOS Apple M5): LATENCY WIN 1.35x-1.94x lower one-way p50 vs UDP loopback (largest for small payloads), p99 comparable-to-better, lower max tail; reliable END-TO-END samples/s is HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK-handshake + poll-granularity bound (NOT SHMEM-bound — UDP baseline itself swings ~10x run-to-run), a direct send-path micro-bench isolates the conditional-wakeup at ~1.4x-1.8x raw send throughput; SHMEM bytes/sample now at the UDP baseline (the per-datagram make-shmem-locator + subseq removed by the dest-cache). NFR-PORT: SBCL has FULL SHMEM on every platform; Clasp/macOS-arm64 -> UDP (shm_open variadic mode_t mispass, shm-attach-by-name-reliable-p NIL, *shmem-enabled* defaults NIL there, SHMEM tests pass-skip cleanly); Clasp/Linux SHMEM EXPECTED via register-varargs ABI, PENDING verification on a Linux host; AllegroCL absent (existing NFR-PORT gap). Remaining transport follow-up: lock-free-MPSC ring + Linux futex fast-path (deferred, measured); Zero-Copy-over-SHMEM (FR-PF-3) reuses this segment + notification machinery. 165 tests green SBCL; gate-types (1043 defuns) + gate-hotpath + fuzz + mem green.

READER_DATA_LIFECYCLE (DDS 1.4 §2.2.3.22): a DataReader purges all internal information + untaken samples for a NOT_ALIVE instance after a configurable delay — autopurge_disposed_samples_delay after it became NOT_ALIVE_DISPOSED, autopurge_nowriter_samples_delay after it became NOT_ALIVE_NO_WRITERS. QoS: two qos-duration slots autopurge-nowriter-samples-delay + autopurge-disposed-samples-delay on dds.qos:qos + make-reader-qos, BOTH default DURATION_INFINITE (the common default is a NO-OP: nothing is ever purged); reader-local, NOT advertised in SEDP, NOT RxO-checked (qos-rxo-compatible unchanged). The instance-rec gains not-alive-since (an internal-time stamp, %lease-now, or nil while ALIVE): set on every ALIVE->NOT_ALIVE transition (%note-not-alive-since, the single stamping point, called from %drain-one-lifecycle for dispose/no-writers AND %on-writer-vanished), cleared on revival to ALIVE (%reader-revive-instance). %autopurge-sweep runs on the DCPS announce cadence (spin, beside %writer-liveliness-sweep, over %participant-readers): for each NOT_ALIVE instance-rec it picks the applicable delay (disposed -> autopurge_disposed_samples_delay; no-writers -> autopurge_nowriter_samples_delay) and, when that delay is finite (not DURATION_INFINITE) AND now-not-alive-since >= the delay (Duration_t->internal-units via %lease-internal-units, the same lease arithmetic the liveliness sweep uses, DRY), PURGES the instance — %autopurge-purge-instance removes its untaken cached samples from dr-cache, its instance-rec from dr-instance-recs (state/gen-counts/writers-set/owner pointer), and its dr-instances view-state entry — so a later sample for the same key starts a brand-new ALIVE instance (view-state NEW, generation counts reset 0). The per-writer dr-drained high-water is intentionally left intact (keyed by writer GUID not instance, RTPS 2.5 §8.3.5.4 — suppresses a replayed lower SN while a fresh higher-SN sample still drains). Mutates dr-cache + instance-recs on the user/spin thread only (the dr-cache owner thread), never the receiver thread (S2 lock discipline). Test dcps-autopurge (deterministic offline injection — stage data + dispose/unregister in the engine SN maps, %drain, BACKDATE not-alive-since past the delay, run %autopurge-sweep, no UDP/no real wait): (a) DEFAULT both-INFINITE never purges a disposed instance (instance-rec + cached samples stay); (b) finite disposed delay -> WITHIN the delay not purged, PAST the delay the instance-rec + cached samples + view-state entry are gone and a new sample for the same key is a FRESH ALIVE instance (view NEW, disposed_generation_count 0); (c) same via the no-writers path under a finite autopurge_nowriter_samples_delay; (d) a disposed-delay reader does NOT purge a NOT_ALIVE_NO_WRITERS instance and a still-ALIVE instance is NEVER purged. REGRESSION: default-INFINITE = no behaviour change — all instance-lifecycle (dcps-instance-state, dcps-no-writers, dcps-disposed-sticky, dcps-drain-sn-order, dcps-autodispose-reader/writer, dcps-writer-unmatch) + ownership + data-plane/SEDP/DCPS tests green. 136 tests green SBCL+Clasp; gate-types + gate-hotpath green.

ENVELOPE: per-store ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS-203) encapsulate -> HKDF-SHA384 DEK (RFC 5869, info='dds-dare/dek/v1') -> AES-256-GCM (SP 800-38D) per record with a 96-bit COUNTER nonce; AAD = topic || writer-guid(16) || sn(8 LE) || kind(1) (authenticated cleartext so the inner store indexes/replays); on-store bytes = version(1) || nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16). NIST/IETF KATs (the conformance oracle, PUBLISHED sources, NEVER self-generated): AES-256-GCM vs NIST SP 800-38D Test Case 16 (run-dare-aes-gcm-kat-test); SHA-384 vs FIPS-180-4 + HKDF-SHA384 vs RFC 5869 (run-dare-sha384-hkdf-kat-test); ML-KEM-1024 vs C2SP/CCTV vectors (run-dare-ml-kem-kat-test). Envelope round-trip + AAD + tamper + wrong-key (run-dare-envelope-test); decorator seal/unseal byte-exact + tamper-drop + delegate (run-dare-encrypted-store-test, run-dare-encrypted-store-lifecycle-test). SECRET HANDLING (owner 'all secrets' directive, conformance): the ML-KEM private key, the shared secret, AND the DEK live in foreign-backed static-vectors (zeroized + freed via free-secret-octets at end-of-life); the DEK is BORN in a static-vector (never transits the heap); secret frees unwind-protect-guarded (throw-safe). KEY-PROVIDER: pluggable closure-vtable (the KMS hook) + default file provider (ML-KEM-1024 keypair, perms enforced 0600/0700 + checked at open, fail-CLOSED on loose OR unverifiable perms, internal decapsulate so the raw private key never leaves the provider); run-dare-key-provider-test. OPEN-PATH FUZZ (NFR-SEC-POSTURE; the operating contract §4): fuzz-dare-open-payload (pbt-test.lisp, 3000 iters) feeds open-payload adversarial sealed blobs (short/oversized/random/all-zero/tampered/wrong-AAD/strictly-truncated-valid + a genuinely-sealed blob under its true AAD) -> NIL or the CORRECT plaintext, NEVER an error/OOB/crash; a (safety 0) arm reaches the same verdict (the bounds guards are explicit manual checks, safety-independent); SKIPs cleanly if OpenSSL<3.5 (the KATs then carry crypto correctness). CROSS-DDS TRANSPARENCY (per-feature DoD, light by nature — DARE adds ZERO wire surface): in-process authoritative proof run-dare-service-transparency-test (a DARE-wrapped service delivers byte-correct retained samples to a same-stack late-joiner; SBCL + Clasp, Clasp first). LIVE foreign-peer confirmation (interop/durability-dare/, 2026-06-19, BOTH peers): a DARE-wrapped durability service delivered byte-correct samples to LIVE TL late-joiners — CONNEXT 7.3.1 received 352 (service retained 403), FAST DDS 3.6.1 received 152 (= 152 collected) — and both captures match the plain-store transient wire BYTE-FOR-BYTE (replay EntityId 0x00000102, firstAvailableSeqNumber=1 held on every HEARTBEAT, CDR_LE (0x0001) on all DATA, NACK->retransmit). NFR-MEM: make mem stays 0.0000 (DARE is control-plane, off the measured CDR hot path) -> no bench. SBOM/PROVENANCE: OpenSSL pinned in scripts/generate-sbom.py + recorded in docs/provenance.md (Apache-2.0, vetted crypto). CLASP DETERMINISM via the PAL (clasp#1793 avoided): DARE secret buffers alloc/free through the impl-agnostic dds.pal:alloc-static/free-static (NOT static-vectors:free-static-vector directly) -- on Clasp free-static recycles into a lock-guarded zero-on-reuse pool, never the buggy interior-pointer GC_FREE of clasp#1793 that corrupts the Boehm heap; on SBCL it truly frees (same workaround the hot-path static buffers already use). DARE validates DETERMINISTICALLY on both SBCL 283 and Clasp 283 (10/10 runs each, zero SIGSEGV); secrets zeroized (fill 0) before release + re-zeroed on reuse; the cosmetic gc_interface.cc:128 printf is gone (free-static-vector no longer on the secret path). Gates: make test (SBCL + Clasp), gate-hotpath, gate-types, mem(0.0000), fuzz, wire — all PASS.
